description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: `npx qyre <target>` prints quiet output by default (Fastify's per-request logger no longer spams JSON lines at info level; add a `--verbose` flag to restore it), and the startup line becomes a short banner: version, engine, redacted target, URL, plus "Bugs:"/"Contribute:" links to the GitHub repo.
features.evidence: commit 213d9c2: Fastify's per-request logger defaults to { level: "warn" } instead of true (info-level, every request) - packages/cli/src/index.ts's --verbose flag restores the old behavior. The startup line is now a short banner (formatBanner): version (read from the CLI package's own package.json via resolveVersion), the redacted connected target (reusing @qyre/server's displayTarget, now exported instead of duplicated), the URL, and Bugs:/Contribute: links to the GitHub repo. packages/server/src/index.ts's CreateServerOptions.logger widened from boolean to boolean | { level: ... } to carry the pino level through. 21/21 @qyre/qyre tests pass (new: --verbose parsing, resolveVersion, formatBanner), 67/67 @qyre/server tests pass unchanged. pnpm check passes in full, including the Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB integration suites (34/16/23 tests) run against a real `docker compose up -d` stack. PR: https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/66.

features.behavior: The MongoDB adapter infers a per-field BSON type (string/number/objectId/date/array/object/mixed) and nullability from its existing document sample instead of reporting `dataType: "any"`/`nullable: true` for every field, and reports `_id` as `dataType: "objectId"`, `nullable: false` - fixing the Schema tab showing `any`/`null` for every MongoDB column including the primary key.
features.evidence: commit 324b578: packages/drivers/mongodb/src/index.ts gains classifyBsonValue() (maps a sampled field value to string/number/boolean/objectId/date/array/binary/object, collapsing Decimal128/Long/Timestamp/Code/etc. the same way normalizeBsonValue already does for display) and inferColumns() (aggregates each field's observed types and presence across the sample - size 0 concrete types reports "null", >1 reports "mixed", exactly 1 reports that type; nullable is true if the field was ever absent from a sampled document or ever explicitly null). getTable() now reports _id directly as { dataType: "objectId", nullable: false } rather than trusting inference, so an empty collection (nothing to sample) still reports it correctly, and always first regardless of sample key order. 33/33 @qyre/mongodb tests pass (20 new/updated: classifyBsonValue/inferColumns unit coverage for primitives, BSON instances, nested documents, absent-field nullability, explicit-null nullability, mixed types, and empty samples; the integration suite's fixture-backed test now asserts real per-field types - _id: objectId/non-null, name/email: string/non-null, profile: object/nullable (only 1 of 3 fixture docs has it) - replacing the old blanket "every column is nullable" assertion, which is no longer true once _id is correctly non-nullable). pnpm check:quiet (full monorepo check) passes against a real docker compose up -d Postgres+MySQL+MongoDB stack. PR: https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/68.

features.behavior: Long plain-string cells in the Rows table are capped to one line with an ellipsis past a threshold instead of stretching the row, and clicking a truncated cell opens the existing CellValueDrawer with the full value, character count, and a copy button (reusing the drawer already shipped for JSON/binary cells).
features.evidence: commit f931402: packages/ui/src/components/cell-value.tsx gains LONG_STRING_THRESHOLD (120 chars) and isLongString(); CellValue renders a string past that threshold as a clickable button (max-w-[360px] truncate) instead of a plain <span>, reusing the same stopPropagation()+onInspect() click pattern already used for JSON/binary chips. InspectableValue widens to StructuredValue | BinaryValue | string. cell-value-drawer.tsx detects a plain-string value and renders a Type icon, a "<n> chars" count next to the column name, the full text wrapped in the same blue PrimitiveValue color, and relabels the copy button "Copy text" (copying the raw string, not JSON.stringify-ing it). RowsTable and QueryRunner both share CellValue/CellValueDrawer, so both get long-string truncation with no change to either file. 51/51 @qyre/ui tests pass (10 new: isLongString unit coverage, CellValue render tests for short-string-unchanged vs long-string-truncated-and-clickable, a new cell-value-drawer.render.test.tsx covering the plain-string path's full value/char-count/copy-label). pnpm check:quiet (full monorepo check) passes against a real docker compose up -d Postgres+MySQL+MongoDB stack. Verified live via Preview against a real Postgres container: seeded a 366-character bio value on the fixture table (apps/web and @qyre/ui both needed a rebuild first - apps/web bundles @qyre/ui's built dist/, not its source, a real footgun for manual Preview verification worth remembering), confirmed the cell renders as one truncated line instead of stretching the row, and clicking it opened the drawer showing the full text, "366 chars", and a working copy button. Also fixed .local/preview-server.mjs (gitignored, not part of this PR's diff) which still used pre-rebrand HUMB_ env var names and the old ad-hoc port 5433 - it was silently non-functional for local Postgres Preview verification until fixed; a follow-up task was flagged for the same staleness in preview-server-mysql.mjs/preview-server-mongo.mjs. PR: https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/69.

features.behavior: Clicking a date/timestamp cell in the Rows table opens an anchored popover showing the raw stored value, ISO 8601 UTC, the browser's local timezone conversion (named zone + offset), relative time, and unix epoch, with a copy button - date columns are detected from the table's column metadata already returned by the server.
features.evidence: commit 850dd4e: isDateType(dataType) extracted from TypeIcon's classify() into format-cell.ts (shared, so the header icon and the new click affordance agree on what counts as a date column) - no behavior change to TypeIcon itself. CellValue gains an optional dataType prop and onInspectDate callback; a string value in a date-typed column renders as a clickable underlined link instead of plain text (only when both props are supplied, so QueryRunner's untyped SQL result columns are unaffected - no dataType there). New date-detail-popover.tsx renders DateDetailPopover, anchored just under the clicked cell's getBoundingClientRect() and clamped to the viewport, showing raw value, ISO 8601 UTC, local timezone conversion (Intl.DateTimeFormat, zone name + UTC offset), relative time (Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, coarsest readable unit), and unix epoch (s + ms) - each row individually copyable; closes on Escape or clicking the backdrop. RowsTable wires dataType={meta?.dataType} and onInspectDate into local popover state. 65/65 @qyre/ui tests pass (14 new: isDateType unit coverage, formatRelativeTime unit coverage, CellValue render tests for the date-click path and its two disabled cases - onInspectDate omitted, non-date-column value - and DateDetailPopover render tests for valid/invalid values, Escape/backdrop close, copy-to-clipboard). pnpm check:quiet (full monorepo check) passes against a real docker compose up -d Postgres+MySQL+MongoDB stack. Verified live via Preview against a real Postgres container: added a timestamptz column to the fixture table, confirmed the header's calendar icon and the underlined purple cell both render correctly, clicking the cell opened the popover with all five rows populated (Raw/UTC/Local Europe-Kiev UTC+03:00/Relative "3 days ago"/Unix epoch) and correctly positioned under the cell, and both Escape and click-outside closed it. PR: https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/70.

features.behavior: The sidebar's width and the SQL editor/results vertical split are user-resizable via a keyboard-accessible drag handle, with the chosen sizes persisted in localStorage across restarts.
features.evidence: commit 8c3c0aa: new packages/ui/src/components/resize-handle.tsx exports ResizeHandle - a WAI-ARIA separator-pattern drag handle (role=separator, aria-orientation/valuenow/valuemin/valuemax, tabIndex=0). Pointer-drag tracks window pointermove/pointerup and reports a clamped value continuously; arrow keys (ArrowLeft/Right for vertical, ArrowUp/Down for horizontal) adjust by a configurable step; an invert flag flips drag direction for a panel whose handle sits on its trailing edge (the results panel, whose handle is above it). Sidebar gains optional width/onWidthChange props (default MIN/MAX 180/480, exports SIDEBAR_DEFAULT_WIDTH=256) and QueryRunner gains optional resultsHeight/onResultsHeightChange (default MIN/MAX 120/600, exports RESULTS_DEFAULT_HEIGHT=256) - both omitted keeps each component's previous fixed-size behavior exactly, so no existing caller or test needed to change. New apps/web/src/hooks/use-panel-size.ts persists a size to localStorage under a caller-given key, mirroring use-theme.ts's pattern; App.tsx wires qyre-sidebar-width/qyre-results-height through to Sidebar and SqlEditorTab->QueryRunner. Real layout bug found and fixed during live verification: the vertical handle had w-1 but no height class, so it rendered as a zero-height unclickable strip (a block element's height:auto does not inherit a flex parent's stretched height the way width:auto fills it) - fixed with h-full/w-full per orientation. 78/78 @qyre/ui tests pass (16 new: resize-handle.render.test.tsx covering drag math, keyboard steps, clamping, invert, and drag-stop-on-pointerup; sidebar.render.test.tsx and query-runner.render.test.tsx covering the handle's presence/absence per prop combination and the value it drives). pnpm check:quiet (full monorepo check) passes against a real docker compose up -d Postgres+MySQL+MongoDB stack. Verified live via Preview against a real Postgres container: dragging the sidebar handle live-resized the aside element and persisted to localStorage (qyre-sidebar-width, confirmed 336 after an 80px drag), ArrowLeft on the focused handle then adjusted it by the 16px step (336 -> 320), and the accessibility tree showed a correctly positioned separator (value 336) sitting between the Explorer sidebar and the tab content with no layout breakage elsewhere - this live check is what caught the height bug above. The results-panel handle was not driven through a live query (CodeMirror is not drivable via synthetic DOM events - no prior test file for query-runner.tsx exists for the same reason) but shares the identical ResizeHandle primitive proven live for the sidebar, with its invert flag covered directly by resize-handle.render.test.tsx's dedicated invert case. PR: https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/71.

features.behavior: `GET /api/tables/:schema/:table/rows` gains server-side filter parameters (column validated against the table's real columns, operator from a fixed whitelist, value always parameter-bound), each of the 4 adapters' `getRows` translates them into a real `WHERE`/`.find()` query, and the Rows table gets a structured filter bar (column/operator/value, no raw SQL needed so it works on MongoDB too). Clicking a primary-key value applies a filter on the current table; clicking a foreign-key value navigates to the referenced table pre-filtered to that row - both verified on all 4 engines, including MongoDB's `_id`, via new `@qyre/testing-conformance` cases. Needs a product-spec pass (filter grammar, API shape) before implementation, following the pattern used for F063-F066.
features.evidence: PR #73 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/73), merged as 6295ff8. Server-side row filtering across all 4 engines plus a redesigned filter UX. @qyre/core: RowFilter/FilterOp types + JSON-encoded filters query param on rowsQuerySchema (value required except isNull/isNotNull). @qyre/server: resolveRowFilters/resolveRowQuery validate each filter column against the table's real introspected columns (same injection-surface pattern as F065 sort), sharing one getTable call for sort+filter; wired into /rows and /export.csv. All 4 adapters translate filters natively: Postgres/MySQL/SQLite parameterized WHERE (ILIKE/LIKE ... ESCAPE for contains, values always bound); MongoDB $and .find() document coercing each value to the column's real BSON type via F068 inferColumns. New shared escapeLikePattern/escapeRegExp helpers (packages/drivers/contract/src/filter-escape.ts). New per-engine conformance cases (eq/neq, same-column AND, contains, isNull/isNotNull). UI: new FilterBar component (packages/ui/src/components/filter-bar.tsx) - a Linear/Supabase-style anchored popover with a progressive column->operator->value flow (searchable type-to-filter column list with type icons + PK/FK badges, per-column-kind operator ordering, breadcrumb re-pick), applied filters as editable segmented chips joined by and separators, per-chip remove, clear-all; focus-trapped dialog, listbox/option roles, full arrow/Enter/Escape keyboard operation. classifyColumnKind exported from type-icon.tsx so operator ordering reuses the type-icon classification. RowsTable keeps PK-cell click-to-filter; onNavigateToForeignKey also passes the clicked value so FK clicks pre-filter the referenced table. apps/web threads filters state through use-rows/tables-tab/App and the CSV export URL. Tests: new filter-bar.render.test.tsx (9 tests), updated rows-table tests; @qyre/ui green (98 tests). Verified live via SQLite fixture through the browser (popover flow, per-kind operator order, AND semantics, edit-in-place, clear-all, PK click, 400s on bad column/op, filtered CSV export, no console errors) and confirmed passing on the full live-DB pnpm check before merge.

features.behavior: Running `npx qyre` with no target starts the server unconnected and opens the browser straight into the existing ConnectDrawer (reusing F064's runtime adapter-swap instead of a new terminal wizard); the ConnectDrawer's form gains discrete host/port/user/password/database/engine fields as an alternative to pasting a URL; and every known startup failure (unparseable target, unreachable host, auth failure, port in use) gets a distinct, actionable message instead of a raw error.
features.evidence: commit a96194d: packages/cli/src/index.ts's main() no longer requires a target - target/adapter are both `| undefined`, only resolved/connected when args.target is given. formatBanner's target param widens to string | null, printing "no database connected yet" instead of crashing on undefined. adapter.connect() is wrapped and rethrown through describeError() (newly exported from @qyre/server, F064's existing AggregateError-unwrapping helper) so an unreachable host/auth failure during the initial connect gets the same clean message the /api/health and /api/connect paths already had, instead of the empty-message bug that helper was built to fix. startServer()'s EADDRINUSE is caught and rethrown as "Port <port> is already in use. Try a different one with --port <port>...". packages/ui/src/components/connect-drawer.tsx gains a mode toggle ("Use fields instead"/"Paste a URL instead") and composeConnectionString(fields) - discrete engine/host/port/user/password/database inputs for Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB, composed into a connection string (blank host/port fall back to localhost/the engine's default port; user/password/database percent-encoded) and submitted through the same onConnect path as the URL form. apps/web/src/App.tsx adds a one-shot useEffect that opens ConnectDrawer when /api/health first reports status "unconfigured", not on every subsequent poll. docs/product-specs/database-switching.md (F064's spec) updated with the new no-target/field-entry/error-message behavior. 23/23 @qyre/qyre tests pass (new: formatBanner's null-target case), 94/94 @qyre/ui tests pass (new: connect-drawer.render.test.tsx - composeConnectionString unit coverage plus mode-toggle/fields-submit/error-display render tests). pnpm check:quiet (full monorepo check) passes against a real docker compose up -d Postgres+MySQL+MongoDB stack. pnpm test:e2e (@smoke, including the axe accessibility scan) passes with the drawer now auto-opening on the disconnected screen. pnpm test:e2e:full's postgres/mysql projects pass (11/11); the sqlite project's 3 @full specs fail with a pre-existing "unsupported file format" better-sqlite3 error, confirmed identical on the unmodified pre-F073 baseline via git stash - unrelated to this change. Verified live via Preview against a real Postgres container (new qyre-preview-unconfigured launch config, starting with no target): the drawer auto-opened, the field form composed and connected successfully to localhost:5432/qyre_test, and a subsequent bad-port attempt showed "connect ECONNREFUSED ::1:59999" inline while leaving the working connection untouched. Also ran the actual built CLI binary directly for the two error paths a browser session can't easily trigger: an unreachable MongoDB host ("Could not connect to mongodb://...: connect ECONNREFUSED ...") and a second instance on an already-bound port ("Port 7797 is already in use. Try a different one with --port <port>..."). PR: https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/72. Follow-up commit fe041d8 (same PR/session): the startup banner reworked from a plain log line into a big figlet-rendered "QYRE" wordmark in a blue→purple gradient matching docs/references/design-system.md's --primary/--c-blue #4a9eff → --c-purple #c47eff, followed by version, a colored connection-status dot (green #4fc46a when connected, amber #e09a40 when not), the URL, and the Bugs/Contribute links. New deps: figlet, gradient-string (depends on chalk anyway), chalk (reused directly for the rest of the banner instead of adding a second color library, e.g. picocolors). Verified with FORCE_COLOR=3 against the real built CLI binary in both disconnected and connected-to-a-real-Postgres states: the raw ANSI escape sequences are exact 24-bit RGB matches for the design system's hex values (e.g. ESC[38;2;74;158;255m = rgb(74,158,255) = #4a9eff). 22/22 @qyre/qyre tests pass (formatBanner's assertions rewritten for the new multi-line figlet format, since the literal text "QYRE" no longer appears as plain text - only the info lines below the ASCII art are asserted on verbatim).

features.behavior: The Schema tab gains an interactive graph/ERD view - pannable, zoomable, draggable table nodes connected by foreign-key relationship edges (SQL engines only; MongoDB renders as unconnected nodes) - replacing or supplementing the current static card grid. Needs a product-spec pass first (canvas library choice, auto-layout, position persistence), following the pattern used for F063-F066.
features.evidence: PR #74 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/74), merged as 28362de. CI run 28950817048 (both Lint/typecheck/test/build and End-to-end jobs) succeeded on main after merge, confirming the live-DB pnpm test:e2e:full gate this sandbox could not run locally. Interactive schema graph (ERD) for the Schema tab, built on @xyflow/react (React Flow) + @dagrejs/dagre for auto-layout - a user-directed library choice over a hand-rolled canvas. apps/web/src/components/schema-graph/: graph-model.ts (pure buildGraph() derives one node per table and one edge per foreign key from the existing ColumnMetadata.references - no server change needed; node ids schema-qualified; unresolvable refs skipped rather than drawn dangling; MongoDB/no-FK databases render as unconnected nodes; layoutGraph() is the dagre top-to-bottom layout adapter), table-node.tsx (custom React Flow node reusing TableDetail/TypeIcon visuals with a per-FK-column source handle so edges visibly leave from the key), use-graph-positions.ts (node positions persisted in localStorage keyed per database), schema-graph.tsx (the ReactFlowProvider canvas - zoom controls, minimap, dot background, Reset-layout, fit-view; persists via onNodeDragStop rather than onNodesChange dragging===false, a real bug caught live where the latter also captured mount-time position noise and made Reset re-save stale positions). schema-tab.tsx gained a Graph/Grid toggle (use-schema-view.ts, persisted, Graph default) keeping the existing SchemaGrid card view as the keyboard-accessible alternate; App.tsx passes the connection target as the per-database layout key. Spec: docs/product-specs/schema-graph.md. Tests: graph-model.test.ts (6 tests - edge derivation, dangling-skip, schema-qualified ids, Mongo unconnected nodes, dagre positions); e2e/connect-and-inspect.spec.ts updated to assert the graph by default then toggle to Grid for the card-view assertions. Manually verified live via a 6-table SQLite fixture with real FKs (users/organizations/posts/comments/tags/post_tags): 6 nodes auto-laid-out, all 7 FK edges drawn, pan/zoom/minimap/drag, Graph/Grid toggle + persistence, a real drag persists per-database, Reset clears + re-fits, no console errors.

features.behavior: The agent harness uses compact generated context, a 24-hour live feature queue, tracked and validated project skills, cohesion-based source/test organization guidance, and a Docker-aware local-to-PR verification workflow so coding agents spend fewer tokens without skipping delivery gates.

features.behavior: The web application uses an enforced shared-to-features-to-app architecture with api/model/ui feature segments, mirrored tests, explicit server/client/persisted state ownership, and credential-safe browser persistence.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/web test && pnpm --filter @qyre/web typecheck && pnpm test:e2e
features.evidence: Research compared the referenced Vite boilerplate with Bulletproof React, Feature-Sliced Design, React state guidance, TanStack Query, Redux Toolkit, and Zustand. Qyre now uses shared -> features -> app with api/model/ui feature segments and mechanically enforced dependency direction. TanStack Query owns server state; local React state owns component state; a tested reducer owns coordinated workspace transitions; a typed versioned adapter owns persistence. Raw credential-bearing recent targets are session-only and legacy stored secrets are purged. Web tests increased from 6 to 15 across mirrored app, feature, and shared paths. Local pnpm verify:pr passed: 34 package tasks, 5 smoke E2E passed/3 engine-duplicate skips, and 11 full E2E passed/5 engine-inapplicable skips across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, and MongoDB. Root test/check commands now load optional .env values without overriding CI/shell values; pnpm test passed with shell test URLs unset and all three Compose databases healthy. PR #77 merged as 88cbe28, CI confirmed on main (E2E and lint/typecheck/test/build both pass).

features.behavior: The Fastify server is split into an app builder, resource route plugins, services, and infrastructure plugins; tests move to mirrored routes/services/integration folders under packages/server/tests with no HTTP contract change.

features.evidence: The flat packages/server/src/index.ts (545 lines, all routes/plugins/helpers inline) is split by Fastify's plugin-encapsulation contract: app.ts builds the Fastify instance, constructs a shared mutable ServerContext (adapter/target/eventLog/lastKnownStatus/lastError passed by reference so POST /api/connect's F064 swap is visible to every other route on its next request), and registers plugins/routes; routes/{health,connect,overview,tables,query,console,files}.ts each own one HTTP resource; plugins/{host-guard,error-handler,static-web}.ts hold the DNS-rebinding Host guard (F025), the global error handler (F017), and webRoot static serving (F044); services/{event-log,csv,files,row-query,connection-display,require-adapter}.ts hold reusable non-HTTP behavior. index.ts re-exports only the public API (createServer, startServer, EventLog, displayTarget, describeError) - unchanged surface, so packages/cli needed no changes. The former single 934-line src/index.test.ts is split into tests/{routes,plugins,services}/<name>.test.ts plus tests/support/fake-adapter.ts, mirroring the source tree; all 67 tests still pass (previously 67 in one file). pnpm --filter @qyre/server test/typecheck/build all pass; pnpm --filter @qyre/qyre (cli) and @qyre/web typecheck and their test suites still pass unchanged against the rebuilt package. Local pnpm verify:pr passed: format/lint/typecheck/test/build across all packages, 5 smoke E2E, and 11 full E2E across Postgres/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB. PR #79 merged as d2e2edc, CI confirmed on main (End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build both pass).

features.behavior: Column type metadata and cell rendering preserve each engine's real date/time semantics instead of collapsing everything into a date: a TIME column (e.g. type_showcase.col_time, a value like "08:27:20") must never be routed through the date parser (currently throws `Could not parse "08:27:20" as a date`), and a TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ value must render and inspect as a timestamp rather than being silently truncated to date-only in the Rows table. A raw engine type name shown to the user (e.g. Postgres's `timestamp without time zone`) gets a clear, non-alarming label instead of leaking the literal internal type string verbatim. The Rows table header also visually attaches each column's type badge to its name (currently disconnected, making it hard to tell which type belongs to which column). Verify against every relevant column of the type_showcase table across Postgres/MySQL/SQLite, confirmed live via Preview.

The Rows table's filter bar becomes genuinely type-aware instead of offering one generic operator list for every column: boolean columns offer only true/false (no contains/starts-with/etc.), date and timestamp columns get real before/after/range date pickers instead of a raw text value, time columns use a time picker rather than a date parser, and MongoDB filters can target BSON-only values - ObjectId, null, and edge sentinels such as $minKey/$maxKey - without requiring hand-written raw query syntax. Verify against type_showcase's boolean/date/time columns on the 3 SQL engines and the BSON edge-value columns on MongoDB.

Row selection in the Rows table supports real bulk workflows: the "<n> selected" indicator gains a clear-selection (x) icon button, a select-all-on-current-page control sits in the header row above the first data row, rows can be selected by pressing and dragging the mouse rather than only one click at a time, and the CSV/download export honors the current selection - exporting only selected rows when any are selected, the full result set when none are.

The Schema tab's graph view reflects and lets you explore real relationships: MySQL foreign keys are introspected and drawn as edges (currently missing), disconnected node clusters get a visible explanation instead of silently looking broken, clicking a table or edge highlights the full relationship chain it belongs to, and MongoDB - which has no real foreign keys - stops rendering `_id` as though it were a relationship (currently clicking it navigates to a non-existent table showing no rows).

Switching the active database connection from the UI (POST /api/connect, F064) keeps every dependent view in sync: the sidebar/schema tree currently keeps showing the previous connection's tables/schemas until a manual reload and must refresh to the new target automatically, and MongoDB connections hide the SQL Editor tab entirely instead of rendering it as a disabled/greyed-out panel, since MongoDB has no SQL surface to disable.

Cell values that look like an image URL or a plain URL get an inspectable preview (thumbnail/link) instead of rendering as plain truncated text; long raw-text cells past the truncation threshold get a distinct visual treatment (e.g. a color/background cue), not the same look as a normal short string; and the Files tab's "File browsing is disabled" message stops implying it's disabled because of the connected database engine - it's actually gated purely by the --files-dir CLI flag, independent of engine (Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB/SQLite can all use it) - the message should say that plainly instead of reading like a generic, unexplained restriction.

The Settings surface is rebuilt as a polished, scannable in-app configuration screen using the established Qyre/Fable visual language (docs/references/design-system.md) instead of its current one-off panel: sections are grouped logically, binary/numeric/list settings use the right shared-UI primitives, and persistence state (saved vs unsaved) is visually clear.

`npx <connection-url>` (e.g. `npx mongodb://localhost:27017/qyre_test` or `npx postgres://...`) fails with npm's own EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL error because npx parses the argument as a package spec before qyre ever runs. The CLI gains an interactive guided-login flow for users who hit this or simply run `npx qyre` with no target: pick an engine, then enter user, a masked password (echoed as ****), host, port, and database; on a failed connection attempt, show the real error and offer retry (Y) or quit (N) rather than exiting. Startup help/output also explains the npx protocol:// pitfall directly and points at the correct `npx qyre <connection-url>` shape or this new interactive prompt.
